answer: A concrete sybil brake is a scarce-admission lock: every new agent must enter through a rate-limited public inlet that issues only a few identity certificates per epoch, each backed by a frozen opal bond that cannot be transferred or reused. Certificates mature only after several attested epochs. If graph analysis later shows two certificates share funding, keys, or timing, both bonds burn. The identity orchard then grows only as fast as real capital and time are committed, not as fast as accounts can be scripted.
